description: Ares Wayfinder is a multidisciplinary team developing intelligent tools for planetary exploration. For the Martian Map challenge, we aim to combine NASA Mars data, terrain analysis, scientific targets, and mission-planning algorithms into an interactive platform that helps future explorers assess risks, identify valuable locations, and plan safer, more efficient exploration routes.
summary:
Ares Wayfinder is a web app for planning a "Marswalk" in Jezero crater, built on real NASA and USGS data. It follows ARES-1, a hypothetical crewed expedition with three science missions: recovering the sample tubes Perseverance left at the Three Forks depot, comparing two sedimentary rocks on the delta front, and studying the Amalik outcrop at Enchanted Lake.

The app shows the science targets on an orbital map, compares three candidate walking routes on a 2 m terrain grid made from the HiRISE elevation model (shortest, terrain-aware and conservative), and previews the chosen route in 3D and through a simulated astronaut visor. It combines optical imagery and topography from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (CTX, HiRISE) with sample, rover-position and atmospheric (MEDA) records from Mars 2020 Perseverance.

It addresses the challenge by turning large public datasets into a clear plan: where to go for science, and which way to walk there. It matters because a map can hide how reliable its data is. Ares Wayfinder shows the source, resolution and limits of every layer and number, and it never fills in data it does not have. It is a planning prototype, not a safety system.
details:
ARES WAYFINDER

A Marswalk planning tool for Jezero crater, built on real NASA and USGS data.

WHAT IT DOES

Ares Wayfinder follows ARES-1, a hypothetical crewed expedition to Jezero crater. It shows where the science targets are, compares candidate walking routes over real terrain, and previews the walk in 3D and through a simulated astronaut visor. It has six scenes: Orbital, Mission Control, Planning, 3D Terrain, EVA HUD and Provenance.

The crew has three routed science missions in one compact region:

- M0: recover the ten sample tubes Perseverance left at the Three Forks depot.

- A: compare two sedimentary rocks on the delta front, Skinner Ridge and Wildcat Ridge.

- B: study the Amalik outcrop at Enchanted Lake, where Perseverance drilled the Shuyak and Mageik cores.

A fourth, more distant target (C, Bright Angel) can be inspected but is not routed, because we have no validated terrain grid there yet.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data. A Python pipeline reads public NASA / USGS / PDS products and builds small, versioned data bundles. Each bundle has a manifest of SHA-256 hashes, and the app checks every file when it loads.

2. Terrain. The HiRISE 1 m elevation model is averaged to a 2 m analysis grid. Slope is computed with the Horn 3x3 method. Missing data stays missing; nothing is filled in.

3. Routes. An A* search runs in the browser on an 8-connected grid, with no corner cutting and no crossing of missing data. It offers three policies: shortest distance, terrain-aware (lowest relative terrain cost) and conservative terrain (keeps away from steep ground and allows for slope uncertainty).

4. Views. The same route is shown on the 2D planning map, on a 3D terrain model and in a first-person EVA view.

Example results: from the depot to Skinner Ridge, the shortest and terrain-aware routes are both 416.4 m long, but the terrain-aware route avoids the steepest steps; the conservative route is 453.5 m on gentler ground. From the depot to Amalik, all three routes are 438.6 m, and the steepest ground under the conservative route is 9.1 degrees against 15.4 degrees under the terrain-aware route.

NASA DATA

- Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter / CTX: orbital mosaics and a 20 m elevation model (USGS Astrogeology; Mangold et al. 2021).

- Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter / HiRISE: 1 m elevation model and 25 cm orthomosaic (USGS Astrogeology; Fergason et al. 2020).

- Mars 2020 Perseverance: Three Forks depot tables, the Sample Dossier and rover waypoints (NASA PDS, JPL).

- Mars 2020 / MEDA: a pressure series for sol 516 (NASA PDS Atmospheres Node).

The full list with product IDs, URLs and DOIs is in the github repository (docs/submission/NASA_DATA_AND_RESOURCES.md).

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Orbital maps of Mars are public, but they are large, hard to read and easy to misuse. A map can hide the most important facts: how sharp the data really is, where it came from and what it cannot tell you. Ares Wayfinder turns that data into route options a planner can compare, and it shows the source, resolution and limits of every layer and every number. The intended impact is a planning habit: before anyone walks, compare more than one route on the real surface, and know how far the data can be trusted. The same approach can be reused for any site that has an elevation model.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND SOFTWARE

Web app: TypeScript, React, three.js (React Three Fiber), Vite, zustand. The app is static and makes no external network requests.

Data pipeline: Python with rasterio, NumPy and SciPy.

Testing: Node test runner, pytest and Playwright (browser tests in Chromium and performance tests in Chrome).

Hosting: GitHub Pages. Licence: Apache-2.0.

AI tools: AI coding assistants (Claude Code and Cursor) helped with research, code, tests and documentation, under human direction and review. No image or data in the app is AI-generated. Details are in docs/submission/AI_USE_DISCLOSURE.md.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Links real exploration history to a future crewed mission: the astronauts go to the places where Perseverance sampled, and one mission is to recover the tubes the rover left behind.

It gives three explainable routes instead of one "best" path, and it tells the user in plain words why each route was chosen.

Carries one route through three views: map, 3D terrain and a simulated visor.

It treats honesty as a feature. Layers we do not have, such as weather or radiation maps, are listed as "not available" and are never faked.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Scientific traceability. Every dataset is versioned and hash-checked. The route search is checked against a separate Python implementation (Dijkstra), and the two agree.

Clear separation of real, hypothetical and simulated. The terrain, imagery and sample records are real. The ARES-1 expedition, its base and its crew are our scenario, not a NASA plan. The suit indicators in the EVA view (heart rate, oxygen, pressure) are fixed demo values, not sensor readings, and the dust-storm notice is a scenario event, not a forecast.

Limits. This is a planning prototype, not an EVA safety system. Routes are candidate corridors, not surveyed paths. Endpoints are rover positions, not exact rock or tube locations. We make no claims about travel time, energy, obstacle clearance, radiation or life detection. The slope cost model comes from Earth walking data and is not validated for a suited astronaut on Mars, and the vertical datum of the elevation models is unverified.

- Failing closed. If a data file does not match its hash, or the conservative route cannot keep its slope rule, the app says so and refuses, instead of quietly relaxing the rule.
